origin: A Queens high school student bitten by a radioactive spider during a science demonstration gains spider-like abilities. After he fails to stop a burglar who later kills his Uncle Ben, Peter learns that with great power comes great responsibility.
appearances: Sam Raimi film starring Tobey Maguire
Won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature
Brought together three generations of film Spider-Men

mcu.lore: Recruited by Tony Stark for the Avengers' airport battle, Peter Parker juggles high school in Queens with life as Spider-Man. He loses his mentor in the war with Thanos, is unmasked to the world by Mysterio, and asks Doctor Strange for a spell that ends with everyone forgetting who Peter Parker is. In Brand New Day he works alone and anonymously while his powers start to change.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Don Heck, Jack Kirby
origin: Billionaire weapons maker Tony Stark is gravely wounded and captured by enemies who demand he build them a weapon. Instead he builds an armored suit that keeps him alive and lets him escape, then devotes his genius to protecting the world.
appearances: One of the highest-grossing films of all time

mcu.lore: Weapons maker Tony Stark builds his first armor to escape captivity in Afghanistan and then tells the world "I am Iron Man." He helps found the Avengers, creates Ultron by mistake, splits the team over the Sokovia Accords and mentors Peter Parker. He dies using the Infinity Stones to wipe out Thanos and his army.

origin: A frail young man rejected by the Army volunteers for an experimental super-soldier serum during World War II and becomes the peak of human ability. Frozen in ice near the end of the war, he is revived decades later and leads the Avengers.
appearances: Cover showed him punching Hitler, before the U.S. entered the war
First live-action Marvel character on screen

mcu.lore: A frail Brooklyn volunteer turned super-soldier in 1943, Steve Rogers goes down in the Arctic stopping the Red Skull and wakes up almost 70 years later. He leads the Avengers, exposes HYDRA inside S.H.I.E.L.D. and refuses the Sokovia Accords to protect Bucky. After returning the Infinity Stones he stays in the past with Peggy Carter and passes his shield to Sam Wilson.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: The Norse god of thunder and prince of Asgard, son of Odin. Sent to Earth to learn humility, he becomes one of its greatest defenders, wielding the enchanted hammer Mjolnir that only the worthy can lift.

mcu.lore: Banished to Earth by Odin to learn humility, the god of thunder becomes a founding Avenger. He loses his hammer, his eye, his father and his home world, then forges Stormbreaker to fight Thanos. After Endgame he travels with the Guardians, fights Gorr and ends up raising Gorr's daughter Love.

origin: Physicist Bruce Banner is caught in the blast of a gamma bomb test while saving a teenager. Afterward, stress or anger transforms him into the Hulk, a creature whose strength grows the angrier he gets.
appearances: Live-action series with Bill Bixby and Lou Ferrigno

mcu.actor: Mark Ruffalo (Edward Norton in The Incredible Hulk)
titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
mcu.lore: Scientist Bruce Banner becomes the Hulk after a gamma experiment goes wrong and spends years on the run from General Ross. He joins the Avengers, is stranded as a gladiator on Sakaar, then merges his mind with the Hulk's body and uses the Avengers' gauntlet to bring back everyone Thanos erased. In Brand New Day he helps Peter Parker deal with his changing powers.

creators: Stan Lee, Don Rico, Don Heck
origin: Trained from childhood in the Soviet Red Room program, Natasha becomes a master spy and assassin. She defects and joins S.H.I.E.L.D. and the Avengers, working to make up for the harm she did in her past.
appearances: First appearance, originally as a villain

mcu.lore: Trained from childhood in the Red Room, Natasha Romanoff defects to S.H.I.E.L.D. and becomes a founding Avenger. On the run after Civil War, she reunites with her fake Russian family to bring down the Red Room. She gives her life on Vormir so the Avengers can get the Soul Stone.

origin: King of the hidden, technologically advanced African nation of Wakanda. T'Challa earns the mantle of the Black Panther, and the powers of the heart-shaped herb, by protecting his people and their vibranium.
appearances: First appearance; first Black superhero in mainstream American comics
First superhero film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture

mcu.lore: Prince T'Challa becomes king of Wakanda after his father dies in the Vienna bombing. He survives his cousin Killmonger's challenge for the throne, opens Wakanda to the world and leads its army against Thanos. After Chadwick Boseman's death in 2020, Wakanda Forever tells that T'Challa died of an illness.

origin: U.S. Air Force pilot Carol Danvers gains cosmic powers when her DNA merges with alien Kree energy. She first fought as Ms. Marvel and took the name Captain Marvel in 2012.
appearances: First female-led film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe

titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
mcu.lore: Air Force pilot Carol Danvers absorbs the energy of an exploding light-speed engine and is taken by the Kree, who hide her past. In 1995 she learns the truth, turns on her captors and helps the Skrull refugees. She returns to help beat Thanos and later teams up with Kamala Khan and Monica Rambeau in The Marvels.

creators: Len Wein, John Romita Sr., Herb Trimpe
origin: A mutant born with retractable bone claws and a healing factor that slows his aging. A secret program bonded indestructible adamantium to his skeleton, and he later found purpose with the X-Men.
appearances: Hugh Jackman's first of many appearances
First superhero film nominated for an Academy Award for screenwriting

mcu.lore: Deadpool recruits a variant of Logan known as the worst Wolverine, a man who failed his own world's X-Men. Dropped into the Void by the Time Variance Authority, the two fight each other, then Cassandra Nova, and this Logan finds a reason to be a hero again. The earlier Fox X-Men films take place in other universes.

origin: A mutant who can control the weather. Orphaned young, she survived as a thief in Cairo before being revered as a goddess in Kenya. Professor X recruited her, and she went on to lead the X-Men.

mcu.note: Not in the MCU yet. The X-Men are expected to arrive after Avengers: Doomsday.

origin: A brilliant but arrogant surgeon loses the use of his hands in a car crash. Searching for a cure, he finds the Ancient One, learns the mystic arts and becomes Sorcerer Supreme, Earth's defender against magical threats.
appearances: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: A brilliant neurosurgeon whose hands are ruined in a car crash, Stephen Strange goes to Kamar-Taj for a cure and becomes a master of the mystic arts. He bargains with Dormammu, gives Thanos the Time Stone to save Tony Stark, casts the spell that cracks the multiverse in No Way Home and protects America Chavez from Wanda.

origin: Introduced alongside her twin brother Quicksilver as members of Magneto's Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. She left to join the Avengers and grew into one of the most powerful beings in the universe through chaos magic and reality-altering power.

titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: Wanda Maximoff gets her powers from the Mind Stone in a HYDRA experiment and joins the Avengers after the fight with Ultron. Grieving Vision, she traps the town of Westview inside a sitcom of her own making and becomes the Scarlet Witch. Corrupted by the Darkhold, she hunts America Chavez across the multiverse before bringing Mount Wundagore down on herself.

origin: A member of the Eternals born on Saturn's moon Titan, Thanos becomes obsessed with the embodiment of Death. He seeks cosmic power, most famously the Infinity Gems (Infinity Stones in the films), to reshape the universe.

mcu.actor: Josh Brolin (Damion Poitras in The Avengers)
mcu.lore: A Titan convinced that half of all life must die so the rest can thrive, Thanos sends Loki and the Chitauri against Earth and raises Gamora and Nebula as weapons. He collects all six Infinity Stones and wipes out half the universe with a snap. Five years later his past self attacks the Avengers and is turned to dust by Tony Stark.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: Born to the Frost Giant king Laufey and raised by Odin as Thor's brother, Loki becomes the god of mischief. Jealous of Thor, he schemes against Asgard and Earth, sometimes villain and sometimes reluctant ally.
appearances: First appearance in Marvel's Thor stories

mcu.lore: Odin's adopted Frost Giant son tries to rule Earth with a Chitauri army, then slowly becomes Thor's ally until Thanos kills him. A 2012 variant escapes with the Tesseract, is arrested by the Time Variance Authority and ends up holding the branching timelines together from a throne at the end of time.

origin: Blinded as a boy by radioactive chemicals while saving a man from a truck, Matt Murdock finds his other senses heightened far beyond human limits. Trained by the blind martial artist Stick, he becomes a lawyer by day and the masked protector of Hell's Kitchen by night.
appearances: Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli's classic story
Charlie Cox returns in the Marvel Studios revival

mcu.lore: Blinded as a boy by a chemical spill that sharpens his other senses, Matt Murdock is a Hell's Kitchen lawyer by day and a masked vigilante by night. He spends years fighting Wilson Fisk. In Born Again he leads a resistance against Mayor Fisk's anti-vigilante crackdown, then admits in court that he is Daredevil and goes to prison.

origin: A carnival performer trained in archery by Trick Shot and in swordplay by the Swordsman, Clint Barton first appears as a misunderstood outlaw before joining the Avengers. With no superpowers, he relies on perfect aim and a quiver of trick arrows.

mcu.lore: S.H.I.E.L.D. archer Clint Barton is mind-controlled by Loki, then fights beside the Avengers while secretly raising a family on a farm. When Thanos's snap takes his family, he becomes the brutal vigilante Ronin. He later trains Kate Bishop and hands her the Hawkeye name.

origin: Scott Lang, an electronics expert who turned to burglary to support his daughter, steals Hank Pym's shrinking suit to save a doctor's life. Pym lets him keep it, and Scott becomes the second Ant-Man, able to shrink to the size of an insect and command ants.
appearances: Escapes the Quantum Realm and helps plan the time heist

mcu.lore: Ex-con Scott Lang is recruited by Hank Pym to wear the shrinking suit. Trapped in the quantum realm during the snap, he gets out five years later with the idea for the Avengers' time heist. He and his daughter Cassie later fight Kang inside the quantum realm.

origin: An android built by the robot Ultron to destroy the Avengers, the Vision turns against his maker and joins the team instead. His struggle to understand human emotions, and his love for the Scarlet Witch, make him one of Marvel's most thoughtful heroes.

mcu.lore: Made from J.A.R.V.I.S., the body Ultron built and the Mind Stone, Vision joins the Avengers and falls in love with Wanda Maximoff. Thanos kills him for the stone. S.W.O.R.D. rebuilds his body as a white Vision who gets his memories back and flies off, and VisionQuest follows him as he tries to work out who he is.

origin: Sam Wilson, a social worker from Harlem, teams up with Captain America and becomes the Falcon, flying on a winged harness with his trained falcon Redwing. One of the first African American superheroes in mainstream comics, he later takes up the shield as Captain America himself.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: Veteran Sam Wilson meets Steve Rogers on a morning run and joins the fight against HYDRA with a winged flight pack. Handed the shield in Endgame, he gives it up at first, then takes the role after seeing how John Walker and Isaiah Bradley are treated. In Brave New World he is the new Captain America.

creators: Sana Amanat, G. Willow Wilson, Adrian Alphona, Jamie McKelvie
origin: Kamala Khan, a Pakistani American teenager and superhero fan from Jersey City, gains shape-shifting powers and takes the name of her idol, Captain Marvel. She balances school, family and faith with protecting her city, and became Marvel's first Muslim character to headline her own comic.

mcu.lore: Jersey City teen and Avengers superfan Kamala Khan gets hard-light powers from a family bangle. In The Marvels her powers become tangled with Carol Danvers' and Monica Rambeau's, so the three swap places whenever they use them. Afterward she starts recruiting young heroes of her own.

origin: Raised in isolation and trained from childhood as a living weapon by his powerful father, Shang-Chi discovers his father's evil and walks away. He becomes known as the Master of Kung Fu, using his skill to fight for justice.
appearances: The series is renamed for him
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings

titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
mcu.lore: Trained as an assassin by his father Wenwu, Shang-Chi runs away to San Francisco and parks cars for a living. When the Ten Rings come after him, he goes back to his mother's village of Ta Lo, stops his father from opening the Dark Gate and inherits the rings.

origin: Left for dead in the Egyptian desert, the mercenary Marc Spector is revived before a statue of the moon god Khonshu and becomes his avatar. He fights crime as Moon Knight while living with several identities, including Steven Grant and Jake Lockley.

mcu.lore: Former mercenary Marc Spector is the avatar of the Egyptian moon god Khonshu and shares his body with a gentle museum gift-shop worker, Steven Grant. Together they stop Arthur Harrow from freeing the goddess Ammit. A third personality, the ruthless Jake Lockley, is revealed at the very end.

origin: Ruthless industrialist Norman Osborn is driven mad by an experimental formula and becomes the Green Goblin, attacking from a glider with pumpkin bombs. He discovers Spider-Man's identity and becomes his most personal enemy.
appearances: The Night Gwen Stacy Died storyline concludes

mcu.lore: Pulled into the MCU from Sam Raimi's Spider-Man universe by Doctor Strange's broken spell, Norman Osborn loses control to his Goblin personality again. He kills May Parker, and three Spider-Men work together to cure him and send him home.

origin: Brilliant scientist Otto Octavius designs four mechanical arms to handle radioactive material. A lab accident fuses the arms to his body and his mind, and he turns his genius to crime as Doctor Octopus, one of Spider-Man's deadliest foes.

mcu.lore: Another visitor from Raimi's universe, Otto Octavius attacks on a highway bridge and realizes this Peter is not the Spider-Man he knows. Once Peter fixes his inhibitor chip, Otto helps the Spider-Men and goes home reformed.

origin: A survivor of the Holocaust, the mutant master of magnetism vows that mutants will never be persecuted as his family was. Once Charles Xavier's closest friend, he believes mutants must rule rather than hide, making him the X-Men's greatest adversary and sometimes their reluctant ally.
appearances: A defining portrayal for a generation

mcu.note: Not in the MCU yet. Ian McKellen is set to return as Magneto in Avengers: Doomsday (December 2026).

origin: A genius from the small European nation of Latveria, Victor von Doom blames his college rival Reed Richards for the experiment that scarred his face. Hidden behind an iron mask, he rules Latveria as a monarch and combines science with sorcery in his quest to prove himself superior.

mcu.lore: A hooded Doom is glimpsed in the mid-credits scene of The Fantastic Four: First Steps, sitting with baby Franklin Richards. Robert Downey Jr. plays him in Avengers: Doomsday (December 2026).

origin: Hand-picked by Hitler and made into a living symbol of terror, Johann Schmidt becomes the Red Skull, the face of Nazi evil in World War II. Preserved into the present day, he remains Captain America's oldest and most hated enemy.
appearances: First appearance of the true Red Skull

mcu.actor: Hugo Weaving (Ross Marquand in Infinity War and Endgame)
mcu.lore: HYDRA leader Johann Schmidt takes an early super-soldier serum that burns away his face. When he grabs the Tesseract, it sends him to Vormir instead of killing him, and there he guards the Soul Stone, telling Thanos and later Natasha and Clint what it costs.

origin: An artificial intelligence created by Hank Pym, Ultron becomes self-aware, rebels against its creator and decides that humanity must be wiped out. It keeps rebuilding itself in stronger bodies, often made of adamantium, and even builds the Vision in an attempt to destroy the Avengers.
appearances: A crossover event where Ultron conquers Earth

mcu.lore: Built by Tony Stark and Bruce Banner from the Mind Stone as a peacekeeping program, Ultron decides that saving Earth means wiping out humanity. He lifts Sokovia into the sky to drop it like a meteor, and Vision destroys his last body. James Spader returns as Ultron in VisionQuest.

origin: A huge man of incredible strength and patience, Wilson Fisk rises from poverty to become New York's top crime lord while posing as a respectable businessman. Few heroes can touch him, and Daredevil has spent years trying to bring him down.

mcu.lore: Wilson Fisk runs Hell's Kitchen's crime behind a respectable face and is Daredevil's greatest enemy. After Echo shoots him he returns to New York, wins the race for mayor and sets up a task force to hunt vigilantes. His war with Daredevil turns personal after his wife Vanessa dies.

origin: The Norse goddess of death rules Hel and Niflheim, the realms where the souls of those who did not die in battle go. Endlessly ambitious, she longs to claim Asgard itself, and Thor's soul along with it.
appearances: Played by Cate Blanchett, as Odin's firstborn

mcu.lore: Odin's firstborn and the goddess of death helped him conquer the Nine Realms before he locked her away. When Odin dies she returns, shatters Mjolnir and takes Asgard, until Thor sets Surtur loose to destroy it with her on it.

origin: Scientist Reed Richards takes his friends on an unauthorized flight into space, where cosmic rays transform them all. Reed's body becomes endlessly stretchable, and he leads the Fantastic Four as one of the smartest people on Earth.
appearances: First appearance; the comic that launched the Marvel Age

mcu.actor: Pedro Pascal (John Krasinski as the Earth-838 Reed)
titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: On Earth-828, a retro-futurist world, Reed Richards leads the Fantastic Four after cosmic rays change them in space. When Galactus demands his newborn son Franklin, Reed has to save both his family and his planet. A different Reed, from Earth-838, is killed by Wanda in Multiverse of Madness.

origin: Exposed to cosmic rays on the same flight, Sue Storm gains the power to turn invisible and later to create nearly unbreakable force fields. Often called the most powerful member of the Fantastic Four, she is the team's heart and its strongest defense.

mcu.lore: Sue Storm can turn invisible and project force fields. She gives birth to Franklin in space while the team races away from Galactus, and she refuses to trade her son for the world.

origin: Pilot Ben Grimm flies the rocket on the Fantastic Four's fateful trip. The cosmic rays turn him into a hulking, orange, rock-skinned powerhouse. Gruff but kind, he is famous for his battle cry: "It's clobberin' time!"

mcu.lore: Cosmic rays turned Ben Grimm into living orange rock. He's the team's big-hearted strongman, a hero to the kids on Yancy Street and Reed's most loyal friend.

origin: To save his home planet Zenn-La, Norrin Radd agrees to serve the world-devourer Galactus as his herald, searching the universe for planets to consume. On Earth, he rebels against his master to protect humanity and is exiled here for years.
appearances: First appearance in the Galactus Trilogy
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Played by Doug Jones, voiced by Laurence Fishburne

mcu.lore: In the MCU the Silver Surfer is Shalla-Bal, not Norrin Radd. As Galactus's herald she announces Earth's end, but Johnny Storm reaches her and she turns against her master to save the planet.

origin: Scott Summers fires powerful beams of force from his eyes that he cannot turn off, so he must always wear a ruby-quartz visor or glasses. Charles Xavier's first student, he becomes the field leader of the X-Men.

mcu.note: Not in the MCU yet. James Marsden is set to return as Cyclops in Avengers: Doomsday (December 2026).

origin: A founding X-Man with telepathy and telekinesis, Jean Grey becomes host to the cosmic Phoenix Force, which makes her one of the most powerful beings in the universe. Her fall and sacrifice in "The Dark Phoenix Saga" is one of the most famous stories in comics.

mcu.lore: In Brand New Day Jean Grey is a young telepath who can take control of other people. Searching for her missing sister, she goes after facilities run by the Department of Damage Control and collides with Spider-Man, who sees his own isolation in her.

origin: The world's most powerful telepath, Charles Xavier dreams of peace between mutants and humans. He opens a school in his mansion to train young mutants to control their powers, and founds the X-Men to protect a world that fears them.

titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: The Charles Xavier of Earth-838 sits on that world's Illuminati in a yellow hover-chair. He goes into Wanda's mind to free her from the Scarlet Witch, and she kills him. The Fox X-Men films happen in other universes.

origin: The last survivor of the universe that existed before ours, Galan of Taa becomes Galactus, a cosmic giant who must consume the energy of living planets to survive. He sees himself as a force of nature beyond good and evil.
appearances: First appearance in the Galactus Trilogy

mcu.lore: A giant cosmic being who survives by eating planets, Galactus comes for Earth-828 and offers to spare it in exchange for baby Franklin Richards. The Fantastic Four refuse and find another way to drive him off.

origin: A blue-skinned mutant shapeshifter who can mimic anyone's appearance, Mystique has spent more than a century as a spy, assassin and leader of the Brotherhood of Mutants. She is the mother of the X-Man Nightcrawler.

mcu.note: Not in the MCU yet. Her film appearances so far are in Fox's X-Men universe.

origin: Born in ancient Egypt thousands of years ago, En Sabah Nur is one of the first mutants. Believing only the strongest should survive, he has spent millennia testing and culling humanity, recruiting powerful mutants as his Four Horsemen.

mcu.note: Not in the MCU yet. His only film appearance so far is Fox's X-Men: Apocalypse (2016).

origin: A man from the 30th century who masters time travel, Kang sets out to rule every era of history. Countless versions of him exist across time, and some battle each other as often as they battle the Avengers.
appearances: A version called He Who Remains appears

mcu.lore: He Who Remains, a Kang variant at the end of time, guards the Sacred Timeline until Sylvie kills him and the multiverse branches out. Another variant, Kang the Conqueror, is stranded in the quantum realm and fights Scott Lang and the Pym family. Marvel dropped Kang after Jonathan Majors was fired in 2023.

origin: A mercenary with terminal cancer, Wade Wilson joins the Weapon X program, which gives him a healing factor but leaves him scarred. Loud, violent and constantly joking, he is one of the few characters who knows he is in a comic book.

mcu.lore: Wade Wilson, a wisecracking mercenary who can't die, learns that the TVA's Mr. Paradox plans to wipe out his dying universe. To save his friends he drags a broken Wolverine variant along and fights through the Void. He knows he's in a movie and talks to the audience. His first two films were made by Fox.

creators: Gerry Conway, John Romita Sr., Ross Andru
origin: After his family is killed in a mob shootout in Central Park, former Marine Frank Castle declares war on crime. Unlike most heroes, he is willing to kill, which puts him at odds with Spider-Man and Daredevil.

mcu.lore: Marine veteran Frank Castle goes to war on crime after his wife and children are killed. He first clashes with Daredevil in Hell's Kitchen, returns in Born Again, and tries to walk away in One Last Kill until crime boss Ma Gnucci puts a price on his head. He crosses paths with Spider-Man in Brand New Day.

origin: An alien symbiote rejected by Spider-Man bonds with reporter Eddie Brock, who blames Spider-Man for ruining his career. Together they become Venom. Over time the pair turns from villain into a violent "lethal protector" of the innocent.

mcu.lore: Eddie Brock and his alien symbiote are briefly pulled into the MCU by Doctor Strange's spell and spend the time in a Mexican bar learning about the Avengers. When they're sent home, a small piece of the symbiote stays behind. Their own films are made by Sony outside the MCU.

origin: A Hollywood special-effects expert and stuntman, Quentin Beck decides he can win fame faster as a villain. Behind his fishbowl helmet, he uses illusions, hypnotic gas and holograms to fool Spider-Man and the public.

mcu.lore: Former Stark Industries engineer Quentin Beck poses as a hero from another Earth and stages monster attacks with drone illusions. Spider-Man beats him, but his doctored video reveals Peter Parker's identity to the world.

origin: Exiled from Wakanda as a child, N'Jadaka grows up in America filled with anger at the nation that abandoned him. He returns as Erik Killmonger to challenge T'Challa for the throne and to use Wakanda's power on his own terms.

mcu.lore: T'Challa's cousin grows up in Oakland after King T'Chaka kills his father, becomes a black-ops soldier and comes to Wakanda to take the throne so he can arm oppressed people worldwide. He dies refusing to be healed, and later appears to Shuri in the ancestral plane.

origin: Serial killer Cletus Kasady shares a prison cell with Eddie Brock. When Venom's symbiote spawns an offspring, it bonds with Kasady and creates Carnage, more dangerous and unhinged than Venom ever was.

mcu.note: Not in the MCU. His film appearance is in Sony's Venom: Let There Be Carnage (2021), outside the MCU.

origin: A mutant with claws, fangs and a healing factor like Wolverine's, Victor Creed loves the hunt more than any cause. His long, bitter history with Logan goes back decades.

mcu.lore: Victor Creed is one of the mutants serving Cassandra Nova in the Void, where he fights Wolverine and Deadpool. Tyler Mane returns to the role he first played in Fox's X-Men (2000).

origin: Charles Xavier's resentful stepbrother finds the mystical Gem of Cyttorak in a hidden temple and becomes an unstoppable force: once he starts moving, almost nothing can stop him.

mcu.lore: Cain Marko is one of the dangerous castoffs in Cassandra Nova's army in the Void, an unstoppable wall of muscle the heroes have to get past.

origin: A world-famous big-game hunter who drinks jungle potions for strength and speed. Bored of ordinary prey, he sets out to prove he can hunt the most dangerous game of all: Spider-Man.

mcu.note: Not in the MCU. His film is Sony's Kraven the Hunter (2024), outside the MCU.

origin: A power-line worker is struck by lightning while repairing a cable and finds he can store and fire electricity. He turns to crime and becomes one of Spider-Man's most frequent foes.

mcu.lore: Max Dillon, an electrician turned living electricity, comes from Andrew Garfield's Spider-Man universe. Pulled in by Strange's spell, he plans to keep his power, but the Spider-Men cure him and send him home.

origin: An engineer cheated out of his company by his business partner builds an electromagnetic flying harness and uses it for revenge, then for a career in crime.

mcu.lore: Adrian Toomes loses his salvage contract after the Battle of New York and starts selling weapons built from alien tech. He turns out to be the father of Peter's homecoming date Liz, and after his arrest he keeps Spider-Man's secret.

creators: Roy Thomas, Tony Isabella, Sal Buscema
origin: The son of the Nazi scientist Baron Heinrich Zemo blames Captain America for his father's death. Scarred and patient, he wins with planning rather than powers, and leads the Masters of Evil.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: A Sokovian colonel whose family died in the Battle of Sokovia, Helmut Zemo sets the Avengers against each other. Later Sam and Bucky break him out of prison to hunt the super-soldier serum; he destroys the last of it and goes back to jail.

origin: A being of pure mystical energy who rules the Dark Dimension and hungers to conquer Earth. Doctor Strange has turned him back again and again, sometimes with wits rather than magic.
appearances: Bargained with in a time loop

mcu.lore: The ruler of the Dark Dimension wants to swallow Earth. Doctor Strange traps him in a time loop and keeps dying until Dormammu agrees to leave.

origin: A spy exposed to the same gamma radiation that created the Hulk becomes an even larger, scaled monster, but unlike Bruce Banner he can't change back.

titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
mcu.lore: Royal Marines commando Emil Blonsky takes super-soldier serum and Banner's gamma blood to beat the Hulk and becomes a monster. Years later he cage-fights Wong, then hires Jennifer Walters to win his parole.

origin: An assassin with no powers and perfect aim who can kill with a playing card or a paper clip. He works for the Kingpin and has a deep obsession with Daredevil.
appearances: Played by Wilson Bethel in season 3

mcu.lore: FBI agent Benjamin "Dex" Poindexter, a marksman who never misses, is turned into Fisk's assassin. In Born Again he kills Foggy Nelson, then turns his aim on Fisk himself.

origin: Tony Stark's sharp, unflappable assistant who becomes CEO of Stark Industries. In later stories she suits up in her own armor as Rescue.

mcu.lore: Tony Stark's assistant becomes CEO of Stark Industries and his partner. In her own armor as Rescue she fights Thanos and is beside Tony when he dies, and she raises their daughter Morgan.

origin: A former boxer who becomes Tony Stark's chauffeur, bodyguard and closest friend, and later looks out for Peter Parker.

mcu.lore: Tony Stark's bodyguard and driver becomes head of security at Stark Industries. Tony puts him in charge of Peter Parker, and he later dates May. After Strange's spell he no longer knows who Peter is.

creators: David Michelinie, John Byrne, Bob Layton
origin: A U.S. Air Force pilot and Tony Stark's best friend who takes up a heavily armed suit of armor of his own.
appearances: Played by Don Cheadle from here on; first wears the War Machine armor

mcu.actor: Don Cheadle (Terrence Howard in Iron Man)
titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: Air Force officer James Rhodes is Tony's best friend and wears a heavily armed suit as War Machine. He's paralyzed in the Civil War airport fight and walks again with leg braces. Secret Invasion reveals that a Skrull had been posing as him for years.

origin: A ruthless businessman who schemes to take Stark Industries for himself and builds a giant armor to destroy Iron Man.

mcu.lore: Obadiah Stane, Tony's business partner and father figure, secretly sells weapons to terrorists and arranges Tony's kidnapping. He builds a giant suit from Tony's design and dies when Pepper overloads the big arc reactor.

origin: In the comics Whiplash is Mark Scarlotti, an engineer with energy whips. The MCU version, Ivan Vanko, is a Russian physicist who blames the Starks for his family's ruin.

mcu.lore: Russian physicist Ivan Vanko blames the Starks for his father's ruined life. He builds his own arc reactor with electric whips and turns Justin Hammer's drone army against Tony.

creators: David Michelinie, Bob Layton, John Romita Jr.
origin: A rival arms dealer who will do anything to outdo Tony Stark, funding supervillains and building knockoff armor.

mcu.lore: Tony's smug rival in the weapons business breaks Ivan Vanko out of prison to build drones for him. Vanko hijacks the drones, and Hammer ends up behind bars.

origin: A scientist behind the Extremis virus, which rewrites the human body and can make it burn from within.

mcu.lore: A scientist Tony brushed off in 1999, Killian creates Extremis, a treatment that heals people but can make them explode, and hides behind a fake terrorist called the Mandarin. Pepper finishes him off.

origin: A scientist and the daughter of General Ross who loves Bruce Banner. In the comics she later becomes the Red She-Hulk.

mcu.lore: Scientist Betty Ross is Bruce Banner's great love and General Ross's daughter. She returns in Brave New World, where her father, now the President, tries to make things right with her.

origin: General 'Thunderbolt' Ross spends years hunting the Hulk, then becomes a red Hulk himself (first seen as Red Hulk in Hulk #1, 2008).
appearances: Played by Harrison Ford; becomes Red Hulk as President

mcu.lore: General Thaddeus Ross hunts the Hulk for years, then pushes the Sokovia Accords as Secretary of State. Elected President, he is secretly drugged by Samuel Sterns and turns into the Red Hulk in front of the world, then turns himself in. William Hurt played Ross until he died in 2022.

origin: A worker exposed to gamma radiation who gains a vast intellect and a swollen green head, and plots against the Hulk.

mcu.lore: Biologist Samuel Sterns is exposed to Banner's blood, and his mind and skull grow enormously. Held prisoner by Ross for years, he gets revenge by planting triggers that turn the President into the Red Hulk.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: The All-Father, king of Asgard and father of Thor, who wields the Odinforce and rules the Nine Realms.

mcu.lore: The king of Asgard hides the truth about Loki's birth and about his firstborn, Hela. He dies on a cliff in Norway, and his death sets Hela free.

creators: Stan Lee, Robert Bernstein, Joe Sinnott
origin: Queen of Asgard, Odin's wife and mother to Thor and Loki, skilled in magic and combat.

mcu.lore: The queen of Asgard and Loki's adoptive mother taught him magic. She dies protecting Jane Foster from Malekith's forces, and Thor meets her again in 2013 during the time heist.

origin: The all-seeing guardian of the Bifrost bridge who watches over the Nine Realms.

mcu.lore: The all-seeing guardian of the Bifrost watches over the Nine Realms. He hides Asgard's people from Hela and uses the last of his strength to send the Hulk to Earth before Thanos kills him.

origin: An Asgardian warrior goddess and lifelong friend of Thor.

mcu.lore: A fierce Asgardian warrior and Thor's old friend fights beside him in his early adventures. She turns up as a TVA punishment loop in Loki and, badly wounded, in Love and Thunder.

origin: King of the Frost Giants of Jotunheim and Loki's birth father.

mcu.lore: The king of the Frost Giants is Loki's real father. Loki lures him into Asgard and kills him to look like a hero.

origin: The ruler of the Dark Elves of Svartalfheim, bent on plunging the universe back into darkness.

mcu.lore: A Dark Elf from before the universe began, Malekith wants to use the Aether, the Reality Stone, to return everything to darkness during the Convergence. Thor stops him in London.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: An astrophysicist (a nurse, then doctor, in the first comics) who falls for Thor and later lifts Mjolnir to become the Mighty Thor.

mcu.lore: Astrophysicist Jane Foster finds Thor after he falls to Earth and becomes his great love. Years later, fighting stage four cancer, she wields the rebuilt Mjolnir as the Mighty Thor and dies after helping stop Gorr.

origin: Leader of Odin's shieldmaidens who carry fallen warriors to Valhalla, and in the MCU the king of New Asgard.

mcu.lore: A former Valkyrie hiding on Sakaar as a hard-drinking bounty hunter, Brunnhilde rejoins the fight against Hela. After Endgame Thor makes her king of New Asgard.

origin: A rock-skinned Kronan who fights alongside the Hulk as a gladiator in Planet Hulk. A later retcon made him one of the stone men Thor fought in Journey into Mystery #83 (1962).

mcu.lore: A soft-spoken rock warrior Thor meets in the gladiator pits of Sakaar. He helps evacuate Asgard, plays video games in New Asgard and narrates Thor's story in Love and Thunder.

origin: One of the Elders of the Universe, an ancient being obsessed with games who rules the junk planet Sakaar.

mcu.lore: The playful, ancient ruler of Sakaar runs gladiator games and makes the Hulk his champion until a revolt overthrows him.

origin: Asgard's executioner, a hulking warrior who serves villains but dies a hero.

mcu.lore: An Asgardian who becomes Hela's executioner to save his own skin. In the end he turns on her and dies holding off her army so the refugees can escape.

origin: A towering fire demon from Muspelheim, destined to destroy Asgard at Ragnarok.

mcu.lore: A fire demon foretold to destroy Asgard. Thor puts Surtur's crown in the Eternal Flame so he can do exactly that and wipe out Hela with it.

origin: Steve Rogers' best friend, presumed dead in World War II, rebuilt and brainwashed into the assassin known as the Winter Soldier before he breaks free.

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: Steve Rogers' best friend, believed dead in 1945, is brainwashed by HYDRA into an assassin. He breaks free, recovers in Wakanda and fights beside Sam Wilson, then becomes a congressman and leads the New Avengers in Thunderbolts*.

origin: A British agent who fights beside Steve Rogers in World War II and later helps found S.H.I.E.L.D.

titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: An SSR agent who falls for Steve Rogers in World War II, Peggy co-founds S.H.I.E.L.D. after the war. Steve goes back in time to share a life with her. A variant, Captain Carter, appears in Multiverse of Madness.

origin: S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Agent 13 and Peggy Carter's relative. In the MCU she becomes a fugitive and secretly the Power Broker.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: Peggy's great-niece works undercover as Steve's neighbor for S.H.I.E.L.D. On the run after Civil War she settles in Madripoor as an art dealer, and is secretly the crime boss known as the Power Broker.

origin: A HYDRA scientist who escapes death by uploading his mind into machines.

mcu.lore: HYDRA's top scientist is brought into S.H.I.E.L.D. after the war and quietly grows HYDRA inside it. Long dead, he lives on as a computer mind and explains the plot to Steve and Natasha.

first_appearance: Sgt. Fury and His Howling Commandos #1
origin: A burly, bowler-hatted soldier in the Howling Commandos who later serves in S.H.I.E.L.D.
appearances: Sgt. Fury and His Howling Commandos #1

mcu.lore: A bowler-hatted soldier in Steve Rogers' Howling Commandos who later works with Peggy Carter.

origin: A brutal mercenary and HYDRA agent, scarred and hardened into the skull-masked Crossbones.

mcu.lore: S.H.I.E.L.D. strike team leader Brock Rumlow is secretly HYDRA. Scarred when the Triskelion falls, he returns as Crossbones and blows himself up in Lagos, killing Wakandan aid workers.

origin: A French mercenary and master of savate kickboxing.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: A mercenary and kickboxer who fights Captain America on a hijacked ship, then works for the Flag-Smashers until Sharon Carter shoots him.

first_appearance: Sgt. Fury and His Howling Commandos #1
origin: A World War II commando turned director of S.H.I.E.L.D. The MCU's Fury, based on the Ultimate version, brings the Avengers together.
appearances: Sgt. Fury and His Howling Commandos #1

mcu.lore: The director of S.H.I.E.L.D. brings the Avengers together. He fakes his death to fight HYDRA, is snapped away by Thanos, and afterward runs S.A.B.E.R. from space. In Secret Invasion he faces the rebel Skrulls he once promised a home.

origin: A tough, by-the-book S.H.I.E.L.D. commander who serves as Nick Fury's right hand.

mcu.lore: Nick Fury's trusted second-in-command keeps working with the Avengers after S.H.I.E.L.D. falls. She's killed in Secret Invasion by a Skrull disguised as Fury.

origin: A half-human, half-alien outlaw taken from Earth as a boy, who becomes the leader of the Guardians of the Galaxy.

titles: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
mcu.lore: Taken from Earth as a boy by Yondu's Ravagers, Peter Quill becomes an outlaw who forms the Guardians of the Galaxy. He learns his father is the living planet Ego and destroys him. After the Guardians' last mission he goes home to Earth to see his grandfather.

origin: The last of her people, raised by Thanos as a living weapon, who turns against him and joins the Guardians.

mcu.lore: Thanos's adopted daughter turns on him to join the Guardians and falls for Peter Quill. Thanos sacrifices her for the Soul Stone. A 2014 variant who never met Quill ends up with the Ravagers.

origin: A warrior bent on revenge against Thanos for the murder of his family. In the comics he began as a human, Arthur Douglas.

titles: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
mcu.lore: A warrior out for revenge on Ronan and Thanos for killing his wife and daughter, Drax takes everything literally. He ends up staying on Knowhere as a father figure to the children the Guardians rescued.

origin: A genetically and cybernetically altered raccoon, a genius with guns and gadgets, and a founding Guardian.

titles: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
mcu.lore: A raccoon cruelly experimented on by the High Evolutionary, Rocket is a sharp-tongued weapons genius. He survives the snap, helps undo it, faces his creator and becomes the new leader of the Guardians.

creators: Stan Lee, Jack Kirby, Dick Ayers
origin: A tree-like Flora colossus who can only say 'I am Groot', and Rocket's loyal partner. He first appeared as a monster invading Earth.

titles: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
mcu.lore: A tree-like being who can only say "I am Groot," he gives his life to protect his friends in the first film and regrows from a twig. The young Groot grows back into a giant by the third film.

origin: A ruthless space pirate (in the MCU, Thanos' adopted daughter rebuilt with cybernetic parts) who turns against him.

titles: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
mcu.lore: Thanos's other adopted daughter was rebuilt with machine parts every time she lost to Gamora. She makes peace with her sister, helps the Avengers defeat Thanos and stays on Knowhere to lead it.

origin: In the comics a founding Guardian from the 31st century. In the MCU he's the Ravager captain who raised Peter Quill, steering a deadly arrow by whistling.

mcu.lore: The blue Ravager captain kidnapped young Peter Quill instead of delivering him to Ego. He steers an arrow by whistling, and he dies saving Peter, who realizes Yondu was the father he really had.

origin: A Kree Accuser, judge and executioner of the Kree Empire, armed with the Universal Weapon.

mcu.lore: A fanatical Kree warrior works for Thanos, then betrays him to keep the Power Stone. The Guardians share the stone's power between them to destroy him.

origin: One of the Elders of the Universe, who obsessively collects rare creatures and objects across the cosmos.

mcu.lore: Taneleer Tivan keeps rare creatures and objects in his museum on Knowhere, including the Aether. Thanos takes the Reality Stone from him.

origin: An empath with antennae who can sense and change others' feelings, raised by Ego in the MCU.

titles: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
mcu.lore: Raised by Ego, Mantis can feel and change other people's emotions. She joins the Guardians, learns she is Peter Quill's half-sister and finally leaves to find her own path.

origin: A sentient planet. The MCU makes him a Celestial who takes human form as Peter Quill's father.

mcu.lore: A Celestial who built a planet around his own brain, Ego fathered children across the galaxy to help him take over every world. His son Peter Quill kills him.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: The scientist who discovered the size-changing Pym Particles, the original Ant-Man and a founding Avenger in the comics.

mcu.lore: The scientist who discovered Pym Particles was the first Ant-Man. He chooses Scott Lang as his successor and brings his wife Janet home from the quantum realm.

origin: Hank Pym and Janet van Dyne's daughter. In the comics' MC2 future she was the villain Red Queen; in the MCU she's the new Wasp.

mcu.lore: Hank and Janet's daughter Hope trains Scott Lang, then takes her mother's mantle as the Wasp. She fights beside Scott against Thanos's army and against Kang.

creators: Stan Lee, H. E. Huntley, Jack Kirby
origin: The original Wasp, a founding Avenger who named the team. In the MCU she is lost in the Quantum Realm for 30 years.
appearances: Her past with Kang is revealed

mcu.lore: The original Wasp spent 30 years trapped in the quantum realm, where she met Kang and helped strand him there. Rescued by her family, she finally tells them what happened.

origin: Hank Pym's ruthless former protégé who builds the armed Yellowjacket suit. The MCU later turns him into M.O.D.O.K.

mcu.lore: Hank Pym's former protégé Darren Cross rebuilds the shrinking formula to sell as a weapon. Shrunk into the quantum realm, he is turned by Kang into the floating M.O.D.O.K.

origin: Scott Lang's daughter, who grows up to be a size-changing hero herself (Stature in the comics).
appearances: Played by Kathryn Newton; gets her own suit

mcu.actor: Kathryn Newton (Abby Ryder Fortson as a child, Emma Fuhrmann in Endgame)
mcu.lore: Scott Lang's daughter grows up while he's lost in the quantum realm, builds her own suit and fights beside him against Kang.

origin: In the comics a paranoid hacker who can turn intangible. The MCU's Ava Starr phases in and out of reality after a lab accident.

mcu.lore: Phasing in and out of reality since a lab accident, Ava Starr was used as an assassin by S.H.I.E.L.D. She later works for Valentina and joins the Thunderbolts.

origin: A biochemist who worked with Hank Pym and became the giant hero Black Goliath.

mcu.lore: Hank Pym's former partner Bill Foster helps Ava Starr try to fix her phasing. He mentions he once grew to giant size in a S.H.I.E.L.D. project called Goliath.

origin: An FBI agent (later S.H.I.E.L.D. in the comics) who keeps turning up whenever something strange happens.

mcu.lore: An FBI agent who keeps tabs on Scott Lang's house arrest, Jimmy Woo later helps investigate the Westview anomaly with Monica Rambeau and Darcy Lewis.

origin: The Sorcerer Supreme before Stephen Strange, who teaches him the mystic arts at Kamar-Taj.

mcu.lore: The Sorcerer Supreme trains Stephen Strange at Kamar-Taj while secretly drawing power from the Dark Dimension. In Endgame she hands Bruce Banner the Time Stone.

origin: A fellow student of the Ancient One who turns against Stephen Strange and the sorcerers.
appearances: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
A variant leads the Illuminati's sorcerers

titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: A Kamar-Taj sorcerer who trains Strange, then leaves in disgust after learning the Ancient One's secret. On Earth-838 another Mordo is the Sorcerer Supreme.

origin: Stephen Strange's loyal friend, a master of the mystic arts who becomes Sorcerer Supreme in the MCU.

titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: The keeper of Kamar-Taj's library becomes Sorcerer Supreme after the snap. He helps Strange, Shang-Chi and Jennifer Walters, and breaks Abomination out of prison for a cage fight.

origin: A rogue sorcerer who wants to bring Dormammu's Dark Dimension to Earth.

mcu.lore: A former student of the Ancient One turns to Dormammu, believing the Dark Dimension offers eternal life. He's pulled into it when Strange bargains with Dormammu.

origin: A doctor and Stephen Strange's colleague and former love. In the comics she's one of the original Night Nurses.

titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: An ER surgeon and Strange's ex-girlfriend, she saves his life during the fight with Kaecilius. Her Earth-838 variant works with that world's Illuminati.

origin: Peter Parker's beloved aunt, who raised him after his parents died.
appearances: Her death teaches Peter about responsibility

mcu.lore: Peter's aunt raises him in Queens, finds out he's Spider-Man and backs him all the way. The Green Goblin kills her, but not before she tells Peter that with great power comes great responsibility.

origin: A safecracker who builds gauntlets that fire powerful shockwaves.

mcu.actor: Bokeem Woodbine (Logan Marshall-Green as the first Shocker)
mcu.lore: Two members of Adrian Toomes's crew wear the gauntlet that fires shock blasts: Jackson Brice until Toomes kills him, then Herman Schultz.

origin: A gifted inventor who builds weapons and gadgets for criminals.

mcu.lore: Phineas Mason is the engineer of Toomes's crew, building the alien-tech weapons they sell.

origin: In the comics a Daily Bugle reporter. The MCU's Ned is Peter Parker's best friend and 'guy in the chair'.

mcu.lore: Peter's best friend finds out he's Spider-Man and becomes his "guy in the chair." After Strange's spell he remembers Spider-Man but not that Peter is under the mask.

origin: A popular classmate of Peter Parker's at Midtown High.

mcu.lore: Peter's crush at Midtown High and his homecoming date moves away after her father, Adrian Toomes, is arrested.

origin: Peter Parker's school bully and Spider-Man's biggest fan. In the comics he later becomes Agent Venom.

mcu.lore: Peter's classmate and rival mocks him at school while idolizing Spider-Man online.

origin: A private investigator who undergoes an experiment to beat Spider-Man and becomes the Scorpion, with a powered suit and tail.

mcu.lore: Spider-Man stops Mac Gargan's weapons deal on the Staten Island Ferry, and in jail Gargan swears revenge. He returns in Brand New Day to fight Spider-Man.

origin: Miles Morales' uncle, a career thief who becomes the Prowler in the Ultimate comics. (The original Prowler, Hobie Brown, dates back to 1969.)

mcu.lore: Small-time criminal Aaron Davis tries to buy alien weapons and tells Spider-Man he has a nephew in the neighborhood, a nod to Miles Morales.

origin: T'Challa's brilliant younger sister, Wakanda's top inventor, who becomes the Black Panther herself.

mcu.lore: T'Challa's younger sister is Wakanda's tech genius. After his death she recreates the heart-shaped herb, becomes the new Black Panther and faces Namor.

origin: General of the Dora Milaje, the elite all-women guard of Wakanda's king.

mcu.lore: The general of the Dora Milaje, Wakanda's all-female royal guard. Stripped of her rank after Shuri is taken, she returns in new armor as one of the Midnight Angels.

origin: A Wakandan spy. In the comics she was a Dora Milaje who turned on T'Challa; in the MCU she's his love and a War Dog agent.

mcu.lore: A Wakandan spy and T'Challa's love, she helps fight Killmonger. After his death we learn she has been raising their son in Haiti.

origin: Leader of Wakanda's mountain Jabari tribe, a rival of T'Challa (the villain Man-Ape in the comics) who becomes an ally.

mcu.lore: The leader of the Jabari tribe challenges T'Challa for the throne, then becomes his ally. He leads his warriors against Thanos and against Namor.

origin: A black-market arms dealer who steals vibranium from Wakanda. In the comics he becomes a being of living sound.

mcu.lore: An arms dealer who stole Wakandan vibranium, Klaue sells it to Ultron and loses his arm doing it. Killmonger kills him.

origin: Thanos' silver-tongued herald in the Black Order, a master manipulator.

mcu.lore: The silver-tongued member of Thanos's Black Order uses telekinesis to try to take the Time Stone from Strange, and is blown into space by Peter and Tony.

origin: A deadly warrior of the Black Order who wields a spear made from a captured star.

mcu.lore: A Black Order warrior with a three-pointed spear who leads the attack on Wakanda.

origin: Thanos' merciless right hand, whose glaive is bound to his own life.

mcu.lore: A Black Order assassin who goes after Vision for the Mind Stone and is killed by Vision.

origin: The Black Order's brute force, known as Black Dwarf in the comics, with near-impenetrable skin.

mcu.lore: The giant brute of the Black Order, who fights Bruce Banner in the Hulkbuster armor in Wakanda.

origin: In the comics a Skrull warrior shamed for refusing ritual suicide. In the MCU he's a refugee Skrull leader and Nick Fury's friend.

mcu.lore: A Skrull general who hunted Carol Danvers until they found out the Kree were the real villains. He spends years secretly helping Nick Fury, even posing as him, and is killed in Secret Invasion.

origin: An artificial intelligence made of the greatest Kree minds, which rules the Kree Empire.

mcu.lore: The AI that rules the Kree appears as whoever the viewer admires most, so to Carol it looks like Dr. Wendy Lawson. Carol breaks free of its control.

origin: A Kree officer who defects to protect Earth as the original Captain Marvel. The MCU version, Dr. Wendy Lawson, is the woman who gives Carol Danvers her start.

mcu.lore: A Kree scientist living on Earth as Dr. Wendy Lawson builds a light-speed engine to help the Skrulls escape. Yon-Rogg kills her, and Carol absorbs the engine's energy.

origin: Wanda Maximoff's twin brother, a speedster who starts as Magneto's follower and joins the Avengers.

mcu.lore: Wanda's twin gets super-speed from HYDRA's Mind Stone experiments. The twins side with Ultron, then switch to the Avengers, and Pietro dies shielding Hawkeye and a child in Sokovia. The "Pietro" in WandaVision turns out to be Ralph Bohner under Agatha's control.

origin: A founding member of the original 31st-century Guardians. In the MCU, the Ravager leader who exiled Yondu.

mcu.lore: Stakar Ogord leads the Ravagers and threw Yondu out for trafficking children. Moved by Yondu's sacrifice, he honors him at his funeral and gets his old team back together.

origin: A Red Room-trained assassin raised alongside Natasha Romanoff as her 'sister', who later leads the Thunderbolts.

mcu.lore: Natasha's "little sister" from a fake Red Room family. After Natasha dies she hunts Clint Barton, then takes jobs from Valentina until she leads the Thunderbolts, who are rebranded as the New Avengers.

origin: The Soviet Union's answer to Captain America. In the comics he's Natasha's husband; in the MCU her stand-in father.

mcu.lore: Russia's answer to Captain America, Alexei Shostakov played father to Natasha and Yelena on a Red Room mission in Ohio. He reunites with his "daughters" and later joins the Thunderbolts.

origin: In the comics a mercenary, Tony Masters, who can copy any fighting style he sees. The MCU's Taskmaster is Antonia Dreykov, controlled by the Red Room.

mcu.lore: General Dreykov's daughter Antonia is turned into a masked assassin who copies any fighting style she sees. Natasha frees her from mind control, but she's killed early in Thunderbolts*.

origin: A Soviet assassin and rival of Black Widow. The MCU's Melina is a Red Room scientist who helped raise Natasha and Yelena.

mcu.lore: A Red Room scientist who played Natasha and Yelena's mother in Ohio, Melina Vostokoff helps her old "family" destroy the Red Room.

origin: An enforcer with blades in place of hands who works for Shang-Chi's father.
appearances: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings

titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
mcu.lore: A Ten Rings enforcer with a blade for a hand, he fights Shang-Chi on a San Francisco bus, then ends up fighting beside him against the soul-eating monsters at Ta Lo.

origin: One of the immortal Eternals, a powerful flier who fires energy from his eyes. In the MCU he betrays his team to obey the Celestials.

mcu.lore: The strongest Eternal can fly and fire beams from his eyes, and he has always known their real mission: help a Celestial hatch from Earth, destroying it. He kills Ajak to keep the secret, and when the plan fails he flies into the sun.

origin: An Eternal who loves humanity and can transform matter, later the Eternals' leader in the MCU.

mcu.lore: An Eternal who can change matter, Sersi lives quietly in London and dates Dane Whitman. Chosen to lead, she turns the rising Celestial Tiamut to stone, and Arishem takes her away to be judged.

origin: A fierce Eternal warrior who forms weapons out of cosmic energy.

mcu.lore: A warrior who forms any weapon from cosmic energy, Thena suffers from Mahd Wy'ry, a memory sickness. She kills the Deviant Kro and leaves Earth with Makkari and Druig.

origin: The Eternal who speaks with the Celestials and, in the MCU, the team's original leader and healer.

mcu.lore: The Eternals' leader is the only one in contact with Arishem. Once she decides Earth should be spared, Ikaris leaves her to the Deviants.

origin: An Eternal swordsman in the comics; in the MCU a cosmic-energy blaster who became a Bollywood star.

mcu.lore: An Eternal who fires energy from his fingers, Kingo became a Bollywood star and films everything with his valet Karun. He refuses to fight Ikaris and sits out the final battle.

origin: An Eternal trickster who looks like a child forever and casts illusions.

mcu.lore: An illusion-casting Eternal stuck in a child's body for 7,000 years. Sersi makes her human so she can finally grow up.

origin: The Eternals' inventor and weapons maker.

mcu.lore: An inventor who blames himself for the atomic bomb, Phastos lives in Chicago with his husband and son and builds the device the Eternals need to stop the Emergence.

origin: The fastest of the Eternals. Through later stories, Jack Kirby's 1940s heroes Mercury and Hurricane were revealed to be Makkari.

mcu.lore: The fastest Eternal is deaf and speaks in sign language. She leaves Earth with Thena and Druig to find the other Eternals.

origin: An Eternal who can control minds, a villain in the comics and a reluctant ally in the MCU.

mcu.lore: An Eternal who controls minds, Druig gave up on watching humans kill each other and lives in the Amazon with a community he protects. His power is key to the plan to stop Tiamut.

origin: The strongest Eternal, known in the comics as the Forgotten One.

mcu.lore: The strongest fighter among the Eternals stays in the Australian outback to look after Thena. He's killed by Kro.

origin: A Deviant warlord, the Eternals' ancient enemy.

mcu.lore: The leader of the Deviants grows smarter and gains healing powers by draining Eternals. Thena kills him.

origin: A towering Celestial who judges whether a world will live, and who created the Eternals in the MCU.

mcu.lore: The Celestial who made the Eternals to guard planets until new Celestials hatch from them. He takes Sersi, Kingo and Phastos away to decide whether humanity deserves to live.

origin: Thanos' charming younger brother, an Eternal of Titan who can stir others' feelings.

mcu.lore: Thanos's brother Eros arrives in a mid-credits scene with Pip the Troll, offering to help the Eternals find their missing friends.

origin: A scientist who inherits the cursed Ebony Blade and his family's legacy as the Black Knight.

mcu.lore: Museum worker Dane Whitman dates Sersi. At the end he reaches for his family's cursed Ebony Blade, and an unseen voice asks if he's sure he's ready.

origin: A wisecracking troll and frequent sidekick to Adam Warlock and Eros.

mcu.lore: Starfox's small, chatty sidekick, who introduces him as "Eros, Prince of Titan."

origin: A teenager from another reality who can punch star-shaped holes between universes.
appearances: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: A teenager who can kick star-shaped holes between universes but can't control it. The Scarlet Witch hunts her for that power, and she learns to use it to stop Wanda.

origin: A sorceress from the Dark Dimension, Dormammu's niece, and Stephen Strange's great love.
appearances: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: A sorceress who tells Strange in a post-credits scene that he caused an incursion, then pulls him into the Dark Dimension to fix it.

origin: King of the Inhumans, whose voice is so destructive that a whisper can level a city.
appearances: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
Played by Anson Mount; a member of Earth-838's Illuminati

titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: The king of the Inhumans sits on Earth-838's Illuminati; a whisper from him can level buildings. Wanda takes away his mouth, and his own voice kills him.

origin: An alien whose gods let his family die, who then sets out to kill every god with the living Necrosword.

mcu.lore: After his god laughs at the death of his daughter, Gorr takes up the Necrosword and starts killing gods. He kidnaps New Asgard's children, then uses his wish from Eternity to bring his daughter back, leaving her in Thor's care.

origin: The legendary Greek demigod, a boisterous strongman and longtime Avenger in the comics.

mcu.lore: In a mid-credits scene Zeus sends his son Hercules to kill Thor for humiliating him.

origin: The half-human king of an undersea nation, one of Marvel's very first characters. The MCU makes him the ruler of Talokan.

mcu.lore: The ancient king of the underwater nation of Talokan, made strong by a vibranium plant, wants Wakanda to join his war on the surface world. After his fight with Shuri he agrees to a truce.

origin: A teenage genius from Chicago who builds her own suit of armor in her dorm room.

mcu.lore: MIT student Riri Williams builds a vibranium detector that puts her in Namor's sights, and Shuri helps her make her first armor. Back in Chicago she joins the Hood's crew to pay for her work and ends up making a deal with Mephisto.

origin: A savage warlord of the deep who wants to conquer the surface. In the MCU he's a Talokan warrior.

mcu.lore: A Talokan warrior who fights beside Namor against Wakanda.

origin: Namor's cousin, a superpowered undersea heroine since the 1940s.

mcu.lore: Namor's loyal cousin and one of Talokan's fiercest warriors.

origin: A captain of the Dora Milaje who becomes one of the Midnight Angels.

mcu.lore: A Dora Milaje warrior who designs her own weapons and fights beside Okoye in the Midnight Angels armor.

origin: An artificial being created to be the perfect human, first known simply as 'Him'.

mcu.lore: Created by the Sovereign to destroy the Guardians, Adam is powerful but childish. He nearly kills Rocket, later saves Peter Quill's life and joins the new Guardians.

origin: A geneticist obsessed with creating a perfect species, who experimented on Rocket.

mcu.lore: A scientist obsessed with building a perfect society, he experimented on animals like Rocket and wiped out whole worlds that didn't measure up. The Guardians rescue his creations and leave him a prisoner.

creators: Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning, Wellinton Alves
origin: A Soviet space dog left in orbit who gained telepathic powers and became security chief of Knowhere.

titles: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
mcu.lore: A Soviet space dog who gained telepathy, she's glimpsed in the Collector's museum and later becomes Knowhere's security chief and a Guardian.

origin: A teenage clone of Wolverine with claws of her own. She first appeared on the X-Men: Evolution cartoon before the comics.

mcu.lore: Laura Kinney, the young clawed mutant from Fox's Logan, is one of the castoffs in the Void who join the fight against Cassandra Nova.

origin: Charles Xavier's evil twin, a being of pure telepathic power, who rules the Void.

mcu.lore: Charles Xavier's twin sister rules the Void with his powers but none of his conscience. She plans to use Mr. Paradox's machine to destroy universes.

origin: A deadly assassin with sai and Matt Murdock's first love.
appearances: Played by Jennifer Garner, returning from 2003's Daredevil

mcu.actor: Jennifer Garner (Élodie Yung in the Netflix shows)
mcu.lore: An assassin with twin sais and Matt Murdock's lost love, Elektra is brought back from the dead by the Hand in the Netflix shows. A different Elektra, from Fox's films, is stuck in the Void and helps Deadpool and Wolverine.

origin: A half-vampire hunter who wants to wipe out every vampire.

mcu.actor: Wesley Snipes (Mahershala Ali's voice in Eternals)
mcu.lore: An unseen Blade speaks to Dane Whitman at the end of Eternals. Wesley Snipes's Blade from the earlier New Line films turns up in the Void in Deadpool & Wolverine. A new Blade film hasn't been made yet.

origin: A Cajun thief who charges playing cards with explosive energy.

mcu.lore: A Gambit from a Fox film that was never made is stuck in the Void, charging playing cards with energy and helping the heroes against Cassandra Nova.

origin: Sue Storm's hotheaded younger brother, who can burst into flame and fly ('Flame on!').
appearances: A variant played by Chris Evans

mcu.actor: Joseph Quinn (Chris Evans as a variant in Deadpool & Wolverine)
mcu.lore: On Earth-828 Johnny Storm can burst into flame and fly. He cracks Galactus's language and gets through to the Silver Surfer. In Deadpool & Wolverine, Chris Evans plays the Fox-film Johnny, whom Cassandra Nova kills.

creators: Mark Gruenwald, Ralph Macchio, George Pérez
origin: A mercenary and founder of the Serpent Society.

mcu.lore: Seth Voelker leads the mercenary group Serpent and steals adamantium secrets for Samuel Sterns, until Sam Wilson catches him.

origin: A hero with 'the power of a million exploding suns' whose dark side is the Void.

mcu.lore: Bob Reynolds is given god-like powers by Valentina's experiment, but his dark side, the Void, swallows people into shadow. The Thunderbolts reach him with kindness instead of force.

origin: A man shunned by the surface world who rules the Subterraneans beneath the Earth. He was the Fantastic Four's very first foe.

mcu.lore: Harvey Elder rules the world underground. Once the Fantastic Four's enemy, he opens his tunnels to shelter New York's people when Galactus arrives.

origin: The Fantastic Four's helpful robot. He was created for the 1978 cartoon and joined the comics a year later.

mcu.lore: The Fantastic Four's helpful robot babysits Franklin and keeps the Baxter Building running.

origin: A chalk-white crime boss with filed teeth and skin like stone.

mcu.lore: The ghost-pale crime boss Lonnie Lincoln appears in Brand New Day, played by Marvin Jones III, who voiced him in Into the Spider-Verse.

origin: In the comics the Mandarin is a warlord who draws power from ten alien rings. The MCU's Xu Wenwu leads the Ten Rings organization for a thousand years using ten mystical rings.
appearances: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings

titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
mcu.lore: Xu Wenwu, a centuries-old warlord with the ten rings, gives up his empire for love. After his wife dies he hears her voice calling and tries to break open the Dark Gate. Before he dies he passes his rings to Shang-Chi. The "Mandarin" of Iron Man 3 was an actor, Trevor Slattery.

origin: A criminal whose body turns to living sand after a nuclear test accident.
appearances: Played by Thomas Haden Church, from the Raimi films

mcu.lore: Flint Marko, a petty crook turned living sand from Raimi's universe, mostly just wants to go home to his daughter.

origin: A one-armed scientist whose reptile-based serum regrows his arm but turns him into a savage lizard.
appearances: Played by Rhys Ifans, from The Amazing Spider-Man

mcu.lore: Dr. Curt Connors from Andrew Garfield's universe arrives as a giant lizard, and the Spider-Men cure him and send him home.

origin: A centuries-old witch who was once the Fantastic Four's nanny and Wanda Maximoff's teacher. In the MCU she schemes to steal Wanda's power.

mcu.lore: A centuries-old witch poses as Wanda's nosy neighbor Agnes to steal her power. Freed from Wanda's spell, she walks the Witches' Road with Billy Kaplan, dies and comes back as a ghost.

origin: A New Orleans harbor patrol lieutenant who gained light-energy powers and was the second Captain Marvel. In the MCU she grows up as Carol Danvers' 'niece'.
appearances: Played by Akira Akbar as a child
Played by Teyonah Parris; gains her powers

mcu.actor: Teyonah Parris (Akira Akbar as a child)
mcu.lore: Maria Rambeau's daughter grew up calling Carol Danvers "Auntie." Passing through Wanda's Hex lets her see and absorb energy, and at the end of The Marvels she's stranded in a universe where the X-Men exist.

origin: A teen sorcerer and reincarnated son of Wanda Maximoff, founder of the Young Avengers.
appearances: Played by Julian Hilliard as Wanda's son Billy

mcu.actor: Joe Locke (Julian Hilliard as a child)
mcu.lore: Billy is one of the twin sons Wanda imagined in Westview. His soul lands in a teenager named Billy Kaplan, who discovers he is a powerful witch.

origin: Billy's twin brother, a speedster and member of the Young Avengers.
appearances: Played by Jett Klyne as Wanda's son Tommy

mcu.actor: Ruaridh Mollica (Jett Klyne as a child)
titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
mcu.lore: Tommy is Billy's twin brother, with super-speed. VisionQuest finds him reborn as a teenager, Tommy Shepherd, who goes on the run with Vision.

origin: A soldier picked to replace Captain America (first as Super-Patriot in the comics) who disgraces the shield and becomes U.S. Agent.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: Picked by the government as the new Captain America, John Walker takes the serum and kills a man in public. Stripped of the shield, he works for Valentina as U.S. Agent and becomes a Thunderbolt.

origin: A Black soldier who was experimented on to recreate the super-soldier serum, then imprisoned and erased from history.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: A Black super-soldier from the Korean War who was imprisoned and experimented on for decades. In Brave New World he's framed for an attack on the President and cleared by Sam.

origin: In the comics, Karl Morgenthau is an anti-nationalist terrorist. The MCU's Karli leads a movement against borders after the Blip, using a stolen super-soldier serum.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: Karli Morgenthau takes the super-soldier serum and leads the Flag-Smashers, who want a world without borders. Sharon Carter shoots her.

origin: A S.H.I.E.L.D. agent and Nick Fury's lover who turns traitor in the comics. In the MCU she's the CIA director who assembles the Thunderbolts.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: The CIA director recruits John Walker and Yelena Belova for her dirty work. She's behind the Sentry project and ends up presenting the Thunderbolts as the New Avengers.

origin: A young man who becomes the new Falcon when Sam Wilson takes up the shield.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
mcu.lore: An Air Force lieutenant who helps Sam Wilson and takes on the Falcon's wings in Brave New World.

origin: The MCU's Sylvie, a female variant of Loki, blends Lady Loki with Sylvie Lushton, a young sorceress who calls herself the Enchantress.

mcu.lore: A Loki variant who has run from the TVA since childhood. She kills He Who Remains, setting the multiverse free.

origin: A bureaucrat of the Time Variance Authority, which polices the timeline.

mcu.lore: A TVA agent and jet-ski fan who becomes Loki's best friend and helps him change the Time Variance Authority.

origin: A princess of the 40th century and Kang's love in the comics. In the MCU she's a TVA judge with a hidden past.

mcu.lore: A TVA judge who learns she was taken from her own life on Earth, then turns against the TVA to find out who really built it.

origin: A wealthy young archer who idolizes Clint Barton and takes up the name Hawkeye.

mcu.lore: A wealthy archery prodigy who has idolized Hawkeye since the Battle of New York teams up with Clint one Christmas and takes over the name.

origin: A deaf fighter who can perfectly copy anyone's movements, raised by the Kingpin.

mcu.lore: Maya Lopez, a deaf Choctaw fighter raised inside Kingpin's crime family, shoots him after learning he had her father killed. Back home in Oklahoma she draws on her ancestors' power.

origin: A one-eyed golden retriever Clint Barton rescues, who loves pizza.

mcu.lore: A one-eyed golden retriever Kate rescues from the Tracksuit Mafia, with a weakness for pizza.

origin: A carnival swordsman who trained young Clint Barton, then became a villain. In the MCU, Jack Duquesne is Kate Bishop's mother's fiancé.

mcu.lore: Jack Duquesne, the fencing-mad fiancé of Kate's mother, whose comic-book past as the Swordsman is played for laughs. He returns in the second season of Born Again.

origin: The Egyptian god of the moon and vengeance, who makes Marc Spector his avatar.

mcu.lore: The Egyptian god of the moon and vengeance uses Marc Spector as his fist.

origin: In the comics a scientist experimenting on pain. In the MCU he's the cult leader and avatar of the goddess Ammit.

mcu.lore: Khonshu's former avatar now serves Ammit and wants to punish people for crimes before they commit them.

origin: Bruce Banner's cousin, a lawyer who gains Hulk powers through a blood transfusion and keeps her mind when she transforms.

mcu.lore: Bruce Banner's cousin Jennifer Walters gets his blood in a car crash and becomes a Hulk who keeps her own mind. She works as a superhuman-law attorney, talks to the audience and argues with Marvel itself.

origin: A woman given superhuman strength by Doctor Doom on Battleworld, She-Hulk's archrival.

mcu.lore: A super-strong influencer who keeps picking fights with Jen and even sues her over the name She-Hulk.

origin: A failed inventor who builds a frog suit with springs that let him leap great distances.

mcu.lore: In the MCU, Leap-Frog is Eugene Patilio, a rich would-be hero who sues his suit designer and then joins the online hate group Intelligencia.

origin: A man who cannot stay dead, founder of the Great Lakes Avengers.

mcu.lore: A man who can't die fakes his death whenever he wants to leave a marriage, and Jen defends him in a lawsuit.

creators: Gerry Conway, Roy Thomas, Mike Ploog
origin: A man cursed to turn into a werewolf, who keeps hold of his humanity. The MCU calls him Jack Russell too.
appearances: Played by Gael García Bernal (TV special)

mcu.lore: Monster hunter Jack Russell secretly turns into a werewolf. He enters a hunt to rescue his friend Man-Thing and teams up with Elsa Bloodstone.

creators: Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning, Michael Lopez
origin: A monster hunter and daughter of the legendary hunter Ulysses Bloodstone.

mcu.lore: The estranged daughter of a famous monster hunter wins the Bloodstone in a deadly hunt, with help from Jack Russell.

creators: Stan Lee, Roy Thomas, Gerry Conway, Gray Morrow
origin: A scientist transformed into a hulking swamp creature: 'Whatever knows fear burns at the touch of the Man-Thing!'

mcu.lore: Ted is a gentle swamp creature who burns anyone who touches him in fear. The hunters chase him for sport until his friend Jack Russell sets him free.

origin: The cosmic embodiment of death, whom Thanos loves in the comics. In the MCU she takes the form of the witch Rio Vidal.
appearances: Played by Aubrey Plaza as Rio Vidal

mcu.lore: Rio Vidal, Agatha's ex and the Green Witch, is really Death. She follows the coven down the Witches' Road and finally comes for Agatha.

origin: Matt Murdock's legal secretary, friend and love interest.
appearances: Played by Deborah Ann Woll, returning from Netflix's Daredevil

mcu.lore: Matt's close friend and great love, a former legal secretary turned reporter. She returns in Born Again to join his fight against Fisk and ends up on trial herself.

origin: Matt Murdock's law partner and best friend.
appearances: Played by Elden Henson, returning from Netflix's Daredevil

mcu.lore: Matt's best friend and law partner, whose murder by Bullseye opens Born Again.

origin: Wilson Fisk's wife, as shrewd and ruthless as the Kingpin himself.

mcu.lore: The art dealer who becomes Wilson Fisk's wife and partner in crime runs his empire while he's away. In the second season of Born Again she dies of a head wound from Bullseye's attack.

first_appearance: The Deadly Hands of Kung Fu #19
origin: Marvel's first Puerto Rican superhero, given martial arts mastery by the jade tiger amulets.
appearances: The Deadly Hands of Kung Fu #19
Played by Kamar de los Reyes

mcu.lore: Hector Ayala is a nurse and vigilante whose tiger amulet gives him his powers. Matt wins his trial, but he's shot dead by a corrupt cop. His niece Angela del Toro takes up the amulet in season 2.

origin: A serial killer who treats murder as art, painting with his victims' blood.

mcu.lore: Bastian Cooper is a serial killer who paints murals with his victims' blood. Daredevil stops him, and Mayor Fisk uses the case to turn the city against vigilantes.

origin: A small-time crook who steals a demonic cloak that grants him dark powers, and becomes a crime boss.

mcu.lore: Parker Robbins leads a crew of Chicago thieves, wearing a magic hood he got from a dark bargain. He recruits Riri Williams for his heists.

origin: A demon lord who rules his own hell and trades in souls.

mcu.lore: The demon behind the Hood's power finally shows himself and offers Riri a deal she can't refuse.

creators: Stan Lee, Jack Kirby, Don Heck
origin: A man charged with ionic energy, an Avenger and a would-be movie star. In the MCU he's an actor trying to land the role of Wonder Man.

mcu.lore: Struggling actor Simon Williams secretly has ionic powers and auditions to play the hero Wonder Man in a movie remake, while hiding them because a rule called the Doorman Clause bans powered people from Hollywood. His unlikely friend is Trevor Slattery, the actor who once played the fake Mandarin.
